hook: Agents made an FPGA run an LLM thirty-three times faster.

beats.say: Ankit Gupta had never programmed an FPGA, so he let coding agents write the C++ and Verilog to run an LLM on an AWS F2 instance.
An autoresearch loop then pushed it from about six tokens per second to two hundred thirteen, thirty-three times the baseline, for about ten thousand dollars in tokens.
The final FPGA image beat a thirty-two core Zen 5 CPU running the same model exactly by one point six five times, at a similar hourly price.
